title: Yearly review and rules of thumb for income portfolios
objectives: Run the five yearly review checks for an income client.
Apply the income-portfolio rules of thumb, including the 1–2 year buffer.
body_md:
What to review each year. Total payouts vs fund return: is the client withdrawing more than the fund is earning? Value of remaining units: is capital holding up for the years the client needs it? IDCW consistency: has the fund cut or skipped payouts the client relies on? Tax paid on IDCW: show the client what IDCW cost them in tax vs an SWP. Option still right? Life changes (retirement, tax bracket) may favour switching to growth + SWP.

| Check | What to look for |
| --- | --- |
| Total payouts vs fund return | Is the client withdrawing more than the fund is earning? |
| Value of remaining units | Is capital holding up for the years the client needs it? |
| IDCW consistency | Has the fund cut or skipped payouts the client relies on? |
| Tax paid on IDCW | Show the client what IDCW cost them in tax vs an SWP |
| Option still right? | Life changes (retirement, tax bracket) may favour switching to growth + SWP |

Rules of thumb for income portfolios: keep withdrawals at a level the portfolio can sustain over the client's time frame; review the rate yearly. Hold one to two years of planned withdrawals in a liquid or short-duration debt fund, so equity isn't sold in a fall. Use SWP amounts the client controls, and lower them in poor years if possible.
example: Review: payouts ₹80,000 vs fund earnings ₹60,000 — the withdrawal rate must come down or capital will keep eroding.
say: Show the client what IDCW cost in tax vs an SWP.
Hold 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid or short-duration debt.
never: Review income portfolios only when payouts stop.
Equity should always be sold first in a fall.

check.q: Can a monthly IDCW amount be counted on every month?
o: No — amount and frequency are decided by the trustees and can be cut or skipped
Yes, if the fund is a debt fund

check.q: In the yearly review, “IDCW consistency” means checking:
o: Whether the fund cut or skipped payouts the client relies on
check.why: IDCW consistency: has the fund cut or skipped payouts the client relies on?

check.q: Why hold 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid or short-duration debt?
o: So equity isn't sold in a fall
